title: Glottis Ltd - 544557 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Glottis is a freight forwarder with FY26 revenue down on softer freight rates and volumes (89,098 TEUs), margins thin at 5.2% PAT, and receivables up about 70% from extended credit days, a weak-quality signal.

summary.headline: Glottis Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 1,959 mn (from INR 1,439 mn in Q3) but PAT margin was 5.5%; FY26 revenue fell to INR 7,226 mn with TEUs down to 89,098.
summary.overview: Glottis reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,959 mn, up sequentially from INR 1,439 mn in Q3 but lower year-on-year, with EBITDA of INR 105 mn (5.4% margin) and PAT of INR 107 mn (5.5% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR 7,226 mn, EBITDA INR 495 mn (6.9% margin) and PAT INR 377 mn (5.2% margin), with management attributing the decline to softer freight rates and lower container volumes. Sea import remained the dominant vertical at about 78% of FY26 revenue, while air and export lines grew from small bases. The balance sheet moved to net cash of INR 510 mn after the IPO. Management was broadly upbeat on FY27 but gave no numerical guidance, and analysts pressed on receivables and falling revenue.

segments.name: Sea import
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at about 73% of Q4 FY26 revenue and about 78% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Sea export
segments.commentary: Contributed about 15% of Q4 and 14% of FY26 revenue, reflecting better traction with export-oriented customers.

segments.name: Air import
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.6% YoY in FY26; share rose to 2.4% from 1.5% in FY25.

segments.name: Air export
segments.commentary: Revenue more than doubled in FY26; share rose to 1.2% from 0.4% in FY25.

segments.name: Road transportation
segments.commentary: Contribution improved to about 5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: End-use sectors
segments.commentary: Renewable energy was the largest contributor at 40.9% of FY26 revenue; automobile share rose to 4.2% from 1.5% (more than doubled); agro products grew 58.7% YoY to 5.7% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue, margin or volume guidance was given for FY27.
Management said it is 'very positive' on FY26-FY27 and is taking measures to recover revenue, without quantifying them.
Stated priorities for FY27: customer engagement, wider sea and air service reach, presence in scalable industries, and selective network expansion.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were disclosed on the call.
Management referred to expanding its operating network and operational infrastructure during FY26 without quantifying it.
Container throughput was 89,098 TEUs in FY26 and 21,356 TEUs in Q4 FY26; the prior-year comparable was not stated on the call.
demand_pricing: Freight rates remained soft and customers planned shipments cautiously due to uneven demand visibility and inventory optimisation.
Volumes fell YoY on slower global trade, inventory correction in major markets and cautious manufacturing procurement.
Asia contributed about 85% of FY26 TEUs, North America about 7%, and Europe about 3%.
Added 163 new customers in FY26; repeat customers rose to 959 from 871.
Top five customers contributed about 33% of revenue, stable YoY.
Management said bunker and crude price moves are passed through via bunker adjustment factor (BAF) and currently have no impact on the business.
Trade receivable days rose, with extended credit days given to customers to retain them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise about 70%, and what drives the increase in other current assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days rose because credit days were extended to customers to retain them amid global volatility and to support expansion; many new customers were added. Other current assets rose due to advances to suppliers and prepaid expenses, since shipping lines and agents are paid early while invoices go out 15-20 days later. No specific receivable or other-asset figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: How do the global crisis and fluctuating oil prices affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude and bunker cost changes are passed to exporters or importers through the bunker adjustment factor, so there is no impact as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did income fall in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited softer freight levels during the year and slower demand as the two main reasons for the revenue decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue decline again in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very positive on FY26-FY27 and is taking many measures to recover revenue, without quantifying them.

risks_watch: Trade receivables rose sharply as credit days were extended; watch collection days and bad-debt risk.
Other current assets rose on supplier advances and prepaid expenses; the breakup was not provided.
Volumes and freight rates were both down YoY; FY26 revenue fell and the FY27 recovery is unquantified.
PAT margin of 5.2% for FY26 is thin, and EBITDA margin for Q4 (5.4%) sits below the FY26 full-year figure (6.9%).
Concentration: top five customers still provide about 33% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and positive about the FY27 outlook, but vague on specifics; management repeatedly attributed the weak year to freight rates and demand and gave no quantified recovery plan. Answers to the receivables question were defensive, framing the rise as deliberate credit extension to retain customers.
key_quotes: We are very positive in FY26-FY27, and we are taking lot of measures to cover up this revenue and we are positive on this.
So, in order to do that, we have given extended credit days, because of that our trade receivables increased.
